question: Does an LLM produce clearer, useful explanations than a fixed template while preserving the same model evidence?
selection: All test students, all three stages; no case exclusion by outcome, confidence, sensitive features or generation quality.
contributors: Up to two largest positive and one largest-magnitude negative Dropout SHAP contributions; ties by original feature name. Same decoded facts in both arms. Baseline/final raw score/remainder retained only in audit files, not writer input.
failure_policy: One generation attempt per case. Save empty, overlength, truncated and failed responses. Resume only cases with no saved record after technical interruption; never retry an existing saved case or select among outputs.

human_review_plan.selection: Smallest SHA256(123:student_key), fixed before inference, all three stages: 180 pairs
human_review_plan.raters_required: At least two independent educational advisers or qualified education researchers; not yet recruited/confirmed
human_review_plan.blinding: Method labels hidden, randomized A/B order per pair; audit integrity separately with supplied evidence. Keep mapping private.
human_review_plan.ratings: Clarity and practical usefulness separately on anchored 1–5 scales; preferred explanation A/B/tie; contributor/value/direction omissions, numerical errors, unsupported claims, causal/probability confusion and missing safeguards as separate flags.

clarity_anchors.1: Very difficult to understand or misleading

usefulness_anchors.1: Not useful for understanding this model output
usefulness_anchors.4: Useful for interpreting the supplied model evidence
usefulness_anchors.5: Highly useful while preserving limitations; not a rating of intervention effectiveness

human_review_plan.A_B_order_rule: LLM is A if the first hexadecimal digit of SHA256('123:blind:'+case_id) is even; otherwise template is A. Mapping retained privately, not given to raters.
human_review_plan.primary_endpoint: Mean paired LLM-minus-template clarity difference on preselected 60 students, averaging raters then three stages within student.
human_review_plan.secondary_endpoints: Usefulness difference, preference/tie proportions, error/omission rates, per-stage results and subgroup descriptive checks.
human_review_plan.inference: 2000 paired student-cluster bootstrap resamples, seed 123, percentile 95% intervals. Resample students, retaining their stages and method pairs. Stage-specific results secondary; no independent-sample analysis of 1326 records.
human_review_plan.missingness: Report recruitment/completion and every missing rating or generation. Never call a missing/failed output correct. Primary clarity comparison uses students with all planned paired ratings; report denominator and sensitivity summaries for all available pairs and generation failure rates.

limits: Prompt revised on validation pilot only; no further pilot requested. No guarantee of final compliance.
The prediction benchmark/test set was previously examined; this is held-out explanation evaluation relative to prompt development, not a new independent predictive validation.

This is verbalization of deterministically decoded and direction-labelled evidence, not an LLM test of inferring SHAP signs from scratch. Public-dataset exposure during LLM pretraining cannot be ruled out.
No claims of causality, improved retention, intervention effectiveness, predictive accuracy gains, calibrated risk or distance-education validity.
Automatic text checks are screening, not proof of semantic correctness; human evaluation is required for clarity/usefulness claims.
